annotations.text:
Three redesign directions for cards at the back, each shown on Home, Practice and Take challenge. Everything is clickable: subject filters, flipping the card, rating it, and answering questions.

Pick a direction (or mix parts of them) and I'll carry it to every screen.

A · Index Card
Grows out of today's look: parchment and ink, Cormorant and DM Sans, brass and ink-violet accents. Every card is a real ruled index card with the red top rule.

For: keeps the brand, calm and literary, cheap to ship.
Tradeoff: the quietest option. Decks still sit in a browse grid, and progress and due cards stay in the background.

B · Night Desk
Dark, dense, keyboard-first. A library table puts mastery and due counts up front, Practice shows a session queue, and every action has a key.

For: built for people doing daily reviews, and spaced repetition becomes the main thread.
Tradeoff: drops the literary identity, feels like a tool more than a place, and a dark-only look needs a light theme later.

C · Pop Quiz
Loud and playful: hard shadows, thick ink outlines, one color per subject, and challenges built like a game show.

For: the most memorable and shareable option, and it suits challenge links sent to friends.
Tradeoff: the furthest from today's brand, and long card text or dense decks strain the chunky type.
